problemSection.subtitle: TherapyNotes, TheraNest, SimplePractice — built for American practitioners, storing your clients' most sensitive data on US servers. Your College doesn't accept that.

cards.title: US cloud complicates PHIPA compliance

cards.desc: Jane App starts at $54/mo. Owl Practice at $89/mo. Built for 10-clinician groups, not solo practitioners.

clientMgmt.body: Pre-built templates for newcomer trauma, BIPOC mental health, and intersectional frameworks — ready to use, fully customizable.

complianceSection.subtitle: Every architectural decision was made with PHIPA, PIPEDA, and College requirements in mind — not retrofitted, built-in from day one.

points.title: All data stored in Canada (AWS ca-central-1)
points.desc: Client records, session notes, billing — hosted exclusively in Montreal and Toronto data centres. Never routed through or accessible under US CLOUD Act.

points.title: AES-256 at rest · TLS 1.3 in transit
points.desc: Locked notes can’t be edited or deleted, every access is written to a tamper-proof audit log, and two-factor authentication is required for client records.

points.title: College-ready records and documentation
points.desc: Note formats, consent forms, and retention periods aligned with CRPO, OCSWSSW, CPO, and CPSBC requirements. Audit logs for every record access.

points.title: Client consent management built-in
points.desc: Digital consent with timestamped e-signatures. Consent versioning — clients re-consent when your policy changes. Withdrawal recorded and respected automatically.

pricingSection.subtitle: No unit minimums. No surprise fees. Cancel any month.

outcomes.title: Outcome measures
outcomes.intro: Record PHQ-9 and GAD-7 results. Totals, severity and the PHQ-9 item 9 flag are calculated by MentalPath. Administer the validated form with your client; enter their answers here.
outcomes.stem: Over the last 2 weeks, how often has the client been bothered by the following problems?

items: Little interest or pleasure in doing things
Trouble falling or staying asleep, or sleeping too much
Feeling tired or having little energy
Feeling bad about yourself — or that you are a failure or have let yourself or your family down
Trouble concentrating on things, such as reading the newspaper or watching television
Moving or speaking so slowly that other people could have noticed, or the opposite — being so fidgety or restless that you have been moving around a lot more than usual
Thoughts that you would be better off dead, or of hurting yourself in some way
Feeling nervous, anxious, or on edge
Not being able to stop or control worrying
Worrying too much about different things
Being so restless that it is hard to sit still
Feeling afraid, as if something awful might happen

outcomes.riskWarning: Item 9 was endorsed. Follow your suicide risk assessment protocol and document it in the session note.
outcomes.empty: No measures recorded for this client yet.
outcomes.deleteConfirm: Delete this result? Only do this if it was entered in error. The deletion is recorded in the audit log.
